Configure Egress Gateway for External API — Fix Connection Timeout (ServiceEntry resolution: NONE)

The Problem: The anihpj-api needs to call an external payment gateway at api.payment-gateway.com. The security policy requires ALL external traffic to go through the Istio Egress Gateway. The ops team creates a ServiceEntry to register the external service, a Gateway for egress, and a VirtualService to route through the egress. But the API pod gets connection timeout when calling the payment gateway. The ServiceEntry has resolution: NONE (the default) — which means Istio treats the host as an IP address, not a DNS name. Envoy expects the application to resolve DNS itself, but since the egress gateway intercepts ALL traffic, the DNS resolution never reaches the actual DNS server. The payment gateway is unreachable.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab) — Istio mesh practice cluster
1

📋 Deploy anihpj-api with Egress Gateway — ServiceEntry resolution: NONE (CONTAINS THE BUG)

📖 APP STORY: anihpj/jobpost processes payments through an external service at api.payment-gateway.com. The security team mandates that ALL outbound traffic must go through the Istio Egress Gateway for auditing. The platform team creates a ServiceEntry to register the payment gateway, an Egress Gateway, a DestinationRule, and a VirtualService. But the ServiceEntry has resolution: NONE — Istio's default. This tells Envoy "the application will resolve the DNS name to an IP, just pass the traffic through." But since ALL traffic is intercepted by the sidecar and routed through the egress gateway, the DNS resolution chain is broken. Payment processing is completely down — no transactions can be completed.
📁 FILE STRUCTURE for anihpj/jobpost (S30): 
anihpj/
├── 00-namespace.yaml              ← ns anihpj with istio-injection
├── 01-api-deployment.yaml         ← Django API (1 replica)
├── 02-api-service.yaml            ← ClusterIP Service (port 8080)
├── 03-serviceentry.yaml           ← ServiceEntry: BUG: resolution: NONE!
├── 04-egress-gateway.yaml         ← Egress Gateway for outbound traffic
├── 05-destinationrule.yaml        ← DR for egress traffic
└── 06-virtualservice.yaml         ← VS: route external traffic through egress
BASH — Deploy Egress Gateway with wrong ServiceEntry resolution (BUG inside) 
# ============================================
# SCENARIO S30: Egress Gateway — ServiceEntry resolution: NONE (BUG)
# ============================================

# 1. CREATE NAMESPACE AND LABEL FOR INJECTION
kubectl create namespace anihpj
kubectl label namespace anihpj istio-injection=enabled

# 2. DEPLOY API + EGRESS GATEWAY + SERVICE ENTRY (BUG: resolution: NONE)
cat << 'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: anihpj-api
  namespace: anihpj
  labels:
    app: anihpj-api
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: anihpj-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: anihpj-api
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        lifecycle:
          postStart:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh","-c","echo 'API (needs egress) - Pod: '$HOSTNAME > /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html"]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: anihpj-api
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:
    app: anihpj-api
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
---
# ServiceEntry: registers external payment gateway (BUG: resolution: NONE!)
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata:
  name: payment-gateway-ext
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  hosts:
  - api.payment-gateway.com
  ports:
  - number: 443
    name: https
    protocol: HTTPS
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL
  resolution: NONE    # ❌ BUG! NONE = treat as IP, not DNS!
---
# Egress Gateway
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: istio-egressgateway
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:
    istio: egressgateway
  servers:
  - port:
      number: 443
      name: https
      protocol: HTTPS
    hosts:
    - api.payment-gateway.com
    tls:
      mode: PASSTHROUGH
---
# DestinationRule for egress
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: egress-payment-dr
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  host: api.payment-gateway.com
  trafficPolicy:
    loadBalancer:
      simple: ROUND_ROBIN
---
# VirtualService to route through egress
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: egress-payment-vs
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  hosts:
  - api.payment-gateway.com
  gateways:
  - istio-egressgateway
  - mesh
  http:
  - match:
    - gateways:
      - mesh
      port: 443
    route:
    - destination:
        host: istio-egressgateway.istio-system.svc.cluster.local
        port:
          number: 443
  - match:
    - gateways:
      - istio-egressgateway
      port: 443
    route:
    - destination:
        host: api.payment-gateway.com
        port:
          number: 443
EOF
⚠

⚠️ Observe the Error — Spot What's Broken

✗1. From API pod, try to reach payment gateway: kubectl exec deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj -- curl -m 5 https://api.payment-gateway.com/ 2>&1 → Connection timeout or "Could not resolve host"
✗2. Check ServiceEntry resolution: kubectl get serviceentry payment-gateway-ext -n anihpj -o yaml | grep resolution → resolution: NONE
✗3. Check Envoy clusters for the external host: istioctl proxy-config clusters deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj | grep payment → Cluster exists but has no resolved endpoints
✗4. Payment processing is completely down — the API can't reach the payment gateway through the egress.
🔍

🔍 Debug — Find the Root Cause

1Check ServiceEntry resolution mode: kubectl get serviceentry payment-gateway-ext -n anihpj -o jsonpath='{.spec.resolution}'
→ NONE — Istio treats the host as an IP, not a DNS name!
2Check if Envoy has resolved endpoints: istioctl proxy-config endpoints deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj --cluster "outbound|443||api.payment-gateway.com"
→ No endpoints — Envoy can't resolve the DNS name because resolution is NONE!
3Understand resolution modes: NONE = application resolves DNS (default), STATIC = hardcoded IPs, DNS = Istio resolves DNS
→ With resolution: NONE, Istio expects the APP to resolve DNS, but the sidecar intercepts all traffic!
4Check egress gateway logs: kubectl logs deploy/istio-egressgateway -n istio-system --tail=20
→ No connection attempts — traffic never reaches the egress gateway!
5Root cause: The ServiceEntry has resolution: NONE — Istio's default. This tells Envoy "the application will resolve the DNS name to an IP address." But with the sidecar intercepting all traffic, the application's DNS resolution goes through the sidecar which expects the ServiceEntry to handle resolution. Since resolution is NONE, no DNS resolution happens — the hostname is never translated to an IP. Fix: change resolution to DNS so Istio resolves the hostname to IP addresses and provides them to Envoy as endpoints.
🧠 Diagnostic Tenet (Thought Process)
①
Connection timeout → DNS not resolving
②
Check ServiceEntry → resolution: NONE
③
NONE = app resolves, but sidecar blocks
④
Change to resolution: DNS
⑤
Istio resolves DNS → egress works ✅

Tenet: ServiceEntry resolution determines HOW Istio resolves the host to endpoints. NONE (default) assumes the application resolves DNS — but with sidecar traffic interception, this breaks. STATIC uses hardcoded IPs. DNS tells Istio to resolve the hostname itself and provide IPs to Envoy. For external services accessed through egress, always use resolution: DNS.

📟 Command Outputs — ERROR State (BEFORE fix)
$ kubectl get serviceentry payment-gateway-ext -n anihpj -o jsonpath='{.spec.resolution}' NONE ← Istio treats the host as an IP — no DNS resolution!
$ kubectl exec deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj -- curl -m 5 https://api.payment-gateway.com/ 2>&1 curl: (6) Could not resolve host: api.payment-gateway.com ← DNS resolution FAILED — payment gateway unreachable!
📟 Command Outputs — AFTER Fix
$ kubectl patch serviceentry payment-gateway-ext -n anihpj --type=json \ -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/resolution","value":"DNS"}]' serviceentry.networking.istio.io/payment-gateway-ext patched
$ kubectl get serviceentry payment-gateway-ext -n anihpj -o jsonpath='{.spec.resolution}' DNS ✅ resolution: DNS — Istio will now resolve the hostname!
$ istioctl proxy-config endpoints deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj | grep payment api.payment-gateway.com:443 → 34.120.57.55:443 ✅ DNS RESOLVED! Endpoint is now available through the egress gateway!
🔧
BASH — Patch ServiceEntry with DNS resolution 
kubectl patch serviceentry payment-gateway-ext -n anihpj --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/resolution","value":"DNS"}]'

# Verify resolution mode changed
kubectl get serviceentry payment-gateway-ext -n anihpj -o jsonpath='{.spec.resolution}'

# Verify endpoints are now resolved
istioctl proxy-config endpoints deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj | grep payment
✓

✅ Verify — DNS Resolution Active, Egress Gateway Routing External Traffic

After changing resolution: NONE to resolution: DNS, Istio now resolves api.payment-gateway.com to actual IP addresses and provides them as Envoy endpoints. The sidecar can now route traffic through the egress gateway to the external payment service. Payment processing is operational — all transactions flow through the audited egress path.

💡 Key takeaway: ServiceEntry resolution modes: NONE (default, app resolves — breaks with sidecar), STATIC (hardcoded IPs), DNS (Istio resolves). For external services accessed through an egress gateway, ALWAYS use resolution: DNS. The default NONE silently breaks DNS resolution because the sidecar intercepts all traffic and expects the ServiceEntry to handle it.

BASH — copy & paste to clean up 
kubectl delete namespace anihpj
DT1
🌳 DECISION TREE DT1 — Pod Not Injected (No istio-proxy Sidecar)

Pod Shows 1/1 Instead of 2/2 — Istio Sidecar Was Never Injected

The Problem: You deploy anihpj/jobpost into the service mesh, but pods show 1/1 READY instead of 2/2. The istio-proxy sidecar container is missing. Without it: no mTLS, no traffic management, no observability. This is the #1 Istio onboarding issue. Your job: follow this decision tree to find WHY the sidecar wasn't injected and FIX it.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab) — Dedicated Istio practice cluster
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — Pod Shows 1/1 Containers (Sidecar Missing)

📖 APP STORY: The anihpj-web Deployment was just created. All 3 pods show Running but only 1/1 READY. The istio-proxy sidecar should make it 2/2. Where is the Envoy proxy?
kubectl get pods -n anihpj
# Start here: Describe the pod to see why injection didn't happen
kubectl describe pod -n anihpj <pod-name> | tail -30

# Check containers in the pod
kubectl get pod -n anihpj <pod-name> -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[*].name}'



    
🔍 What Does kubectl describe Events Show?

    
    
        
  • No events about injection / "created container" only for app
    → The MutatingWebhook never fired! Go to NODE 2 (Namespace Label)
    • 
        
  • "Failed to create pod sandbox" / "ErrImagePull" on istio-proxy
    → Go to NODE 3 (Image Registry / Network)
    • 
        
  • Events show injection attempt but pod annotation says "false"
    → Go to NODE 4 (Pod-Level Annotation)
    • 
        
  • "error adding pod: no running istiod revision found"
    → Go to NODE 5 (istiod Not Running)
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — Namespace Label: Is istio-injection=enabled Set?

                    

                        

                            

                            

                                
Check namespace labels

                                kubectl get namespace anihpj --show-labels
                            

                        

                        

                            

                            

                                
Check Webhook namespaceSelector

                                kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfiguration istio-sidecar-injector -o yaml | grep -A5 namespaceSelector
                            

                        

                    




    
Namespace Label — Root Cause Matrix

    
    
        
  • Label MISSING entirely?
    The MutatingWebhook only fires for namespaces with istio-injection=enabled. Without it, injection is silently skipped. Label it NOW.
    • 
        
  • Label is istio-injection=disabled?
    Explicitly disabled — change to enabled or remove the label if using revision-based injection.
    • 
        
  • Using revision-based injection (istio.io/rev)?
    If using canary upgrades, the namespace needs istio.io/rev=<revision> instead of istio-injection=enabled. Both methods work but don't mix them.
    • 
        
  • Label exists but webhook namespaceSelector doesn't match?
    Check if the webhook's namespaceSelector expects a different label key. Some custom installs change this.
    • 
    






    
Label namespace AND restart pods (existing pods are NEVER retroactively injected)

    kubectl label namespace anihpj istio-injection=enabled --overwrite
kubectl rollout restart deploy -n anihpj
kubectl get pods -n anihpj     # Should now show 2/2 READY




⚠️ CRITICAL: Existing pods are NEVER retroactively injected! You MUST restart the pods (rollout restart) after labeling the namespace. The sidecar is only injected at POD CREATION time by the MutatingWebhook.
N3

🔴 NODE 3 — Webhook Not Running / Image Pull Issues

                    

                        

                            

                            

                                
Check webhook exists

                                kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfiguration istio-sidecar-injector
                            

                        

                        

                            

                            

                                
Check istiod health

                                kubectl get pods -n istio-system -l app=istiod
                            

                        

                    




    
Webhook & Image Issues

    
    
        
  • MutatingWebhookConfiguration NOT FOUND?
    Someone deleted it! Reinstall: istioctl install --set profile=default -y. The webhook is installed by istiod.
    • 
        
  • istiod pod NOT Running?
    The webhook endpoint is served by istiod. If istiod is down → no injection. Check: kubectl logs -n istio-system deploy/istiod
    • 
        
  • ErrImagePull on istio-proxy image?
    Check proxy image: kubectl get cm -n istio-system istio-sidecar-injector -o yaml | grep image. Is the registry reachable? Air-gapped environment?
    • 
    






    
Reinstall Istio to restore webhook

    istioctl install --set profile=default -y
kubectl rollout restart deploy -n anihpj
N4

🔴 NODE 4 — Pod-Level Injection Annotation

                    

                        

                            

                            

                                
Check pod injection annotation

                                kubectl get pod -n anihpj <pod> -o yaml | grep sidecar.istio.io/inject
                            

                        

                    




    
Pod Annotation Diagnosis

    
    
        
  • sidecar.istio.io/inject: "false"?
    The pod explicitly DISABLES injection. Remove this annotation from the pod template or set to "true".
    • 
        
  • No annotation at all?
    If namespace IS labeled but annotation is missing, the webhook adds it. Check if webhook is actually running (NODE 3).
    • 
        
  • sidecar.istio.io/status has error?
    Check: kubectl get pod -o json | jq '.metadata.annotations["sidecar.istio.io/status"]'. May show injection failure reason.
    • 
    






    
Remove injection-disabling annotation from Deployment

    kubectl patch deploy <name> -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/metadata/annotations/sidecar.istio.io~1inject"}
]'
N5

🔴 NODE 5 — istiod Control Plane NOT Running or Wrong Revision

                    

                        

                            

                            

                                
Check all istiod revisions

                                kubectl get pods -n istio-system -l app=istiod
                            

                        

                        

                            

                            

                                
Check namespace revision label

                                kubectl get ns anihpj --show-labels | grep istio.io/rev
                            

                        

                    




    
istiod Health — Revision Mismatch?

    
    
        
  • istiod pod NOT Running (CrashLoopBackOff / Pending)?
    Check logs: kubectl logs -n istio-system deploy/istiod. Common: CA cert expired, resource limits too low, ConfigMap corruption. Reinstall if needed.
    • 
        
  • Namespace has istio.io/rev: 1-20 but istiod-1-20 is NOT running?
    Revision was decommissioned during upgrade! Either reinstall revision: istioctl install --set revision=1-20 -y or switch namespace to the running revision.
    • 
        
  • Multi-cluster: istiod on primary cluster not accessible from remote?
    Check east-west gateway and network connectivity between clusters. istiod must be reachable from the remote cluster's API server.
    • 
    






    
Reinstall missing istiod revision or restart istiod

    istioctl install --set revision=1-22 --set profile=default -y
# OR switch namespace to running revision:
kubectl label ns anihpj istio.io/rev=1-22 --overwrite
kubectl rollout restart deploy -n anihpj




⚠️ ICA EXAM TIP: "Pod sidecar not injected after rollback" = old istiod revision was prematurely decommissioned. Always keep the previous revision running for 24-48 hours after canary upgrades.
DT2
🌳 DECISION TREE DT2 — VirtualService 503 "No Healthy Upstream"

curl Returns 503 — VirtualService Not Routing / "No Healthy Upstream"

The Problem: Users report HTTP 503 errors on the anihpj API. The pods are Running and healthy, but Istio returns "no healthy upstream" or "NoRoute". This means the VirtualService can't find matching endpoints. Is it a host mismatch? Port mismatch? Missing subset? Wrong namespace? Follow this tree to systematically eliminate each cause.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab) — Dedicated Istio practice cluster
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — 503 From Service / "No Healthy Upstream"

📖 APP STORY: The anihpj-api was deployed with a VirtualService and DestinationRule. But curl anihpj-api:8080/ returns 503. Pods are Running and healthy. The mesh is operational — other services work fine. What's wrong with THIS VirtualService?
curl -v anihpj-api.anihpj:8080/ 2>&1 | grep "HTTP\|upstream\|503"

    
🔍 503 Root Cause — What's the Error Message?

    
    
        
  • "no healthy upstream" (UH)
    → Envoy found a route but ALL endpoints are unhealthy. Go to NODE 2 (Endpoints)
    • 
        
  • "NoRoute" or "NR"
    → No VirtualService route matched the request. Go to NODE 3 (Route Matching)
    • 
        
  • "connection refused" / timeout
    → Port mismatch or Service not listening. Go to NODE 4 (Port/Service)
    • 
        
  • 200 but WRONG content
    → Wrong pod receiving traffic. Go to NODE 5 (Subset/Label Mismatch)
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — Endpoints: Are Pods Healthy & Matching Service Selector?

                    

                        

                            
Check Service endpoints

                            kubectl get endpoints anihpj-api -n anihpj
                        

                        

                            
Check Envoy cluster endpoints

                            istioctl proxy-config endpoints deploy/<source> -n anihpj --cluster "outbound|8080||anihpj-api.anihpj.svc.cluster.local"
                        

                    



    
Endpoint Health Matrix

    
    
        
  • kubectl get endpoints shows NO endpoints?
    Service selector doesn't match ANY pod labels. Check: kubectl get pods -l <selector> and compare with Service spec.selector.
    • 
        
  • Endpoints exist but Envoy shows them as UNHEALTHY?
    Readiness probe failing? Check pod readiness: kubectl get pods -n anihpj — are they Ready? Envoy only routes to READY pods.
    • 
        
  • Envoy cluster shows 0 endpoints but Service has them?
    Check DestinationRule subsets: do the subset labels match the pod labels EXACTLY? Go to NODE 5.
    • 
    





    
Fix Service selector to match pod labels

    kubectl patch svc anihpj-api -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/selector","value":{"app":"anihpj-api"}}
]'
N3

🔴 NODE 3 — Route Matching: Does the VirtualService Match the Request?


    
VirtualService Route Matching — Check These

    
    
        
  • VirtualService host matches Service FQDN?
    Must match: anihpj-api.anihpj.svc.cluster.local or short anihpj-api. Typos break routing silently.
    • 
        
  • URI match prefix/exact too restrictive?
    Does your request path match any route rule? No match = 503 NoRoute. Add a catch-all.
    • 
        
  • Headers match condition present but missing in request?
    Header-based routing needs the EXACT header. Use curl -H "header: value" to test.
    • 
        
  • Multiple VirtualServices for same host?
    Istio merges them — first VS's routes take priority. Check all namespaces.
    • 
    





    
Add catch-all route to VirtualService

    kubectl patch vs anihpj-api-vs -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"add","path":"/spec/http/-","value":{"route":[{"destination":{"host":"anihpj-api"}}]}
]'
N4

🔴 NODE 4 — Port Mismatch: VirtualService Port vs Service Port


    
Port Number Alignment

    
    
        
  • VirtualService destination port matches Service port?
    Port 80 in VS but Service on 8080? Envoy connects to the VS port — mismatch = connection refused.
    • 
        
  • Gateway port vs VirtualService binding?
    Gateway server port must match the traffic you're sending (80→HTTP, 443→HTTPS).
    • 
        
  • TCP ServiceEntry port vs actual external port?
    ServiceEntry port must match the actual external service port.
    • 
    





    
Fix port in VirtualService destination

    kubectl patch vs anihpj-api-vs -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/http/0/route/0/destination/port/number","value":8080}
]'
N5

🔴 NODE 5 — Subset/Label Mismatch: Wrong Pods Getting Traffic


    
Subset Label Key/Value Check

    
    
        
  • DestinationRule subset labels match pod labels EXACTLY?
    Label KEY must match — version: v2 ≠ app-version: v2. Case-sensitive, key-sensitive.
    • 
        
  • Subset referenced in VirtualService exists in DestinationRule?
    VS routes to subset: v3 but DR only has v1/v2? Subset not found = fallback to default Service.
    • 
        
  • TrafficPolicy at subset-level vs top-level?
    LB/connection pool at SUBSET level only applies when that subset IS referenced in a route.
    • 
    





    
Fix DestinationRule labels to match pods

    kubectl patch dr anihpj-api-dr -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/subsets/0/labels","value":{"app-version":"v1"}},
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/subsets/1/labels","value":{"app-version":"v2"}}
]'
DT3
🌳 DECISION TREE DT3 — mTLS Handshake Failure

Traffic Blocked with TLS Error — mTLS Handshake Fails Between Services

The Problem: Service-to-service communication suddenly fails. curl returns "connection refused," "TLS handshake failed," or "certificate verification error." This is a classic mTLS issue — one side expects TLS, the other doesn't. Maybe PeerAuthentication is STRICT but one side lacks a sidecar. Maybe SPIFFE certificates expired. Follow this tree to resolve the TLS deadlock.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — TLS/mTLS Error Between Services

📖 APP STORY: anihpj-web calls anihpj-api but gets "connection refused." Both pods are Running. The API works when called from a non-mesh debug pod. mTLS is blocking the connection.

    
What's the TLS Error Type?

    
    
        
  • "connection refused" / immediate reset
    → Plaintext sent to TLS port or TLS sent to plaintext. Go to NODE 2 (PeerAuthentication)
    • 
        
  • "certificate verify error" / SAN mismatch
    → SPIFFE cert issue. Go to NODE 3 (Certificates)
    • 
        
  • "handshake timeout"
    → Network issue or Envoy not processing. Go to NODE 4 (Sidecar Health)
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — PeerAuthentication Mode Mismatch


    
Check PeerAuthentication Configuration

    
    
        
  • Mesh-wide STRICT but one service has no sidecar?
    STRICT mode requires ALL services to have sidecars. The non-mesh service can't complete TLS. Fix: inject sidecar or change to PERMISSIVE.
    • 
        
  • Namespace-level PERMISSIVE overriding mesh STRICT?
    Check: kubectl get peerauthentication -A. Namespace policy takes precedence over mesh-wide.
    • 
        
  • Port-level mTLS exclusion?
    Check: kubectl get peerauthentication -o yaml | grep portLevelMtls. Some ports may be excluded from mTLS.
    • 
    




Set mesh-wide mTLS to PERMISSIVE (allows plaintext too)

kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata: {name: default, namespace: istio-system}
spec: {mtls: {mode: PERMISSIVE}}
EOF
N3

🔴 NODE 3 — SPIFFE Certificates Expired or Invalid


    
Certificate Health Check

    
    
        
  • Check Envoy certs: istioctl proxy-config secret deploy/<pod> -n anihpj
    Look for "EXPIRED" or "VALIDATION ERROR". Certs expire after 24h by default — istiod auto-rotates them. If istiod was down for >24h, certs expired.
    • 
        
  • Check CA cert: kubectl get secret -n istio-system istio-ca-secret -o yaml | grep "ca-cert"
    If CA cert expired, ALL mTLS fails. Check expiry: openssl x509 -in ca-cert.pem -noout -dates
    • 
    




Force certificate rotation by restarting istiod

kubectl rollout restart deploy/istiod -n istio-system
kubectl rollout restart deploy -n anihpj
N4

🔴 NODE 4 — Sidecar Not Proxying / Envoy Not Ready


    
Sidecar Health Check

    
    
        
  • Pod shows 2/2 but istio-proxy is restarting?
    Check: kubectl logs -n anihpj <pod> -c istio-proxy. Common: config rejected, memory OOM, or bootstrap failure.
    • 
        
  • iptables rules broken?
    Check: kubectl exec -n anihpj <pod> -c istio-proxy -- iptables -t nat -L. Missing ISTIO_INBOUND/OUTPUT chains?
    • 
    




Restart pod to re-inject sidecar

kubectl delete pod -n anihpj <pod>
kubectl get pods -n anihpj -w
DT4
🌳 DECISION TREE DT4 — Sidecar Config Stale (xDS Sync Not Updating)

istioctl proxy-status Shows STALE — Envoy Not Receiving Config Updates

The Problem: You update a VirtualService but traffic routing doesn't change. istioctl proxy-status shows proxies as STALE. Envoy is running with outdated configuration. New routes, new DestinationRules, new policies — none of them propagate. The mesh appears frozen. Find why xDS sync is broken.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — proxy-status Shows STALE

xDS Sync — What's Broken?

    
    
        
  • ALL proxies STALE?
    → istiod is down or overloaded. Go to NODE 2 (istiod Health)
    • 
        
  • Only SOME proxies STALE?
    → Network issue between those proxies and istiod. Go to NODE 3 (Network)
    • 
        
  • STALE on ONE xDS type only (e.g., just RDS)?
    → Specific config type issue. Check istiod logs for that xDS type push errors.
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — istiod Health & Resources

istiod Diagnosis

    
    
        
  • istiod OOMKilled? kubectl describe pod -n istio-system -l app=istiod | grep OOM
    Too many proxies/configs exhausting memory. Increase limits or reduce mesh scope with Sidecar resource.
    • 
        
  • istiod CrashLoopBackOff? kubectl logs -n istio-system deploy/istiod --tail=50
    Check for cert errors, ConfigMap corruption, or invalid CRDs.
    • 
        
  • istiod Running but CPU throttled?
    Check: kubectl top pods -n istio-system. Increase CPU limits in IstioOperator.
    • 
    




Restart istiod to recover xDS sync

kubectl rollout restart deploy/istiod -n istio-system
kubectl rollout restart deploy -n anihpj
N3

🔴 NODE 3 — Network Between Envoy and istiod (Port 15012)

Network Path Check

    
    
        
  • Can Envoy reach istiod? kubectl exec -n anihpj <pod> -c istio-proxy -- curl -s istiod.istio-system:15012/debug/adsz
    If timeout: NetworkPolicy blocking port 15012? Firewall? DNS resolution failing?
    • 
        
  • NetworkPolicy blocking xDS port?
    Check: kubectl get networkpolicy -A | grep 15012. Ensure istiod port 15012 is allowed.
    • 
    




Allow xDS traffic to istiod

kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: allow-istiod, namespace: istio-system}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: istiod}}
  ingress: [{ports: [{port: 15012}]}]
EOF
DT5
🌳 DECISION TREE DT5 — Kiali Shows "Unknown" Services

Services in Kiali Graph Are Gray/Unknown — Observability Not Working

The Problem: You open Kiali to visualize your service mesh, but several services appear as gray "Unknown" nodes. No traffic metrics, no request rates, no error percentages. The mesh is running but Kiali can't see these services. Is Prometheus scraping broken? Are metrics labels missing? Is the namespace not selected?

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — Kiali Shows Unknown/Gray Services

Why Are Services Unknown in Kiali?

    
    
        
  • Specific services gray, others OK?
    → Prometheus not scraping those services. Go to NODE 2 (Prometheus)
    • 
        
  • ALL services gray?
    → Kiali can't reach Prometheus at all. Go to NODE 3 (Kiali Config)
    • 
        
  • Services show but no metrics?
    → Metrics labels missing or incorrect. Go to NODE 4 (Telemetry)
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — Prometheus Not Scraping Those Services

Prometheus Scrape Check

    
    
        
  • Check Prometheus targets: Port-forward Prometheus and check /targets
    Are the Envoy endpoints listed? If not, ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor might be missing or misconfigured.
    • 
        
  • Check if namespace is selected in Kiali: Kiali only shows namespaces you've selected in the namespace dropdown.
    Simple fix: ensure the namespace is checked in Kiali's namespace selector.
    • 
    




Verify Prometheus can scrape Envoy stats

kubectl port-forward -n istio-system svc/prometheus 9090:9090 &
curl -s http://localhost:9090/api/v1/targets | jq '.data.activeTargets[] | select(.labels.app=="anihpj-api")'
N3

🔴 NODE 3 — Kiali Cannot Reach Prometheus

Kiali-Prometheus Connection

    
    
        
  • Check Kiali config: kubectl get cm -n istio-system kiali -o yaml | grep prometheus
    Is the Prometheus URL correct? Default: http://prometheus.istio-system:9090
    • 
    




Fix Kiali Prometheus URL

kubectl patch cm kiali -n istio-system --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/data/config.yaml","value":"external_services:\n  prometheus:\n    url: \"http://prometheus.istio-system:9090\""}
]'
N4

🔴 NODE 4 — Telemetry/Metrics Labels Missing

Telemetry Configuration

    
    
        
  • Check Envoy stats: kubectl exec deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj -c istio-proxy -- curl -s localhost:15000/stats | grep requests
    Are metrics being generated? If yes, the issue is in Prometheus scraping, not Envoy.
    • 
        
  • Telemetry API overriding defaults? kubectl get telemetry -A
    Check if a Telemetry resource disabled metrics for certain workloads.
    •
DT6
🌳 DECISION TREE DT6 — JWT Authentication Failing (All Requests 401)

JWT Token Rejected — Every Request Returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized

The Problem: You configured RequestAuthentication and AuthorizationPolicy for JWT. But ALL requests return 401 Unauthorized. The JWT token is valid, the JWKS endpoint is reachable, and the policy is deployed. Yet every request is rejected. Is the issuer wrong? Audience mismatch? JWKS URI unreachable from istiod? Follow this tree.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — JWT Requests Return 401

JWT Failure — What's the Symptom?

    
    
        
  • "Jwt verification fails" / "invalid token"
    → Token itself is invalid or expired. Go to NODE 2 (Token Validity)
    • 
        
  • "Issuer not configured" / "no matching issuer"
    → iss claim doesn't match RequestAuthentication issuer. Go to NODE 3 (Issuer)
    • 
        
  • "Jwks fetch error"
    → istiod can't reach the JWKS URI. Go to NODE 4 (JWKS Reachability)
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — Token Expired or Invalid

Token Validation

    
    
        
  • Check token expiry: echo $JWT | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d | jq .exp
    Compare with current time. If expired, generate a new token.
    • 
        
  • Check audience: echo $JWT | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d | jq .aud
    If RequestAuthentication specifies audiences, the token aud MUST match.
    • 
    




Generate new token with correct claims

curl -s -X POST https://auth.example.com/token -d 'grant_type=client_credentials' | jq -r .access_token
N3

🔴 NODE 3 — Issuer Mismatch

Issuer Configuration

    
    
        
  • Check token iss: echo $JWT | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d | jq .iss
    Must EXACTLY match issuer in RequestAuthentication. Trailing slash matters! https://auth.example.com ≠ https://auth.example.com/
    • 
        
  • Check RA config: kubectl get requestauthentication -A -o yaml | grep issuer
    • 
    




Fix issuer in RequestAuthentication

kubectl patch requestauthentication jwt-auth -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/jwtRules/0/issuer","value":"https://auth.example.com/"}
]'
N4

🔴 NODE 4 — JWKS URI Not Reachable from istiod

JWKS Reachability

    
    
        
  • Check if JWKS URI is reachable from cluster: kubectl run test --rm -it --image=curlimages/curl -- curl -s https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
    If timeout: need ServiceEntry for external auth service. If DNS fails: check CoreDNS.
    • 
        
  • istiod uses its own network (not sidecar): istiod doesn't go through the mesh. Ensure the JWKS URI is reachable from the cluster network, not through egress gateway.
    • 
    




Create ServiceEntry for external auth service

kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata: {name: auth-ext, namespace: istio-system}
spec:
  hosts: [auth.example.com]
  ports: [{number: 443, name: https, protocol: HTTPS}]
  resolution: DNS
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL
EOF
DT7
🌳 DECISION TREE DT7 — Egress Traffic Blocked

Cannot Reach External Services — Egress Traffic Silently Blocked

The Problem: anihpj-api needs to call an external payment API, but every request times out. By default, Istio BLOCKS all egress traffic to unknown hosts. You need a ServiceEntry to allow it. But even with a ServiceEntry, traffic might be blocked by AuthorizationPolicy, wrong resolution mode, or missing egress gateway config. Follow this tree to unblock egress.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — External Call Fails

Egress Failure Mode

    
    
        
  • Immediate "connection refused" / reset
    → No ServiceEntry — Istio blocks unknown hosts by default. Go to NODE 2 (ServiceEntry)
    • 
        
  • Timeout / "could not resolve host"
    → DNS resolution issue. Go to NODE 3 (DNS Resolution)
    • 
        
  • 403 Forbidden / RBAC denied
    → AuthorizationPolicy blocking egress. Go to NODE 4 (AuthZ)
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — ServiceEntry Missing or Wrong

ServiceEntry Check

    
    
        
  • ServiceEntry exists? kubectl get serviceentry -A | grep <host>
    If not: create one! Without ServiceEntry, Istio blocks egress to unknown hosts (default meshConfig.outboundTrafficPolicy.mode=ALLOW_ANY or REGISTRY_ONLY).
    • 
        
  • ServiceEntry host matches EXACTLY?
    Wildcards: *.example.com matches api.example.com but NOT api.example.com:443.
    • 
    




Create ServiceEntry for external host

kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata: {name: payment-ext, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  hosts: [api.payment-gateway.com]
  ports: [{number: 443, name: https, protocol: HTTPS}]
  resolution: DNS
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL
EOF
N3

🔴 NODE 3 — DNS Resolution for External Host

DNS Resolution Mode

    
    
        
  • resolution: NONE (default)?
    With sidecar, DNS resolution breaks. Change to resolution: DNS so Istio resolves the hostname.
    • 
        
  • resolution: STATIC but wrong IP?
    Check: kubectl get serviceentry -o yaml | grep address. Static IPs must be correct.
    • 
    




Change ServiceEntry to DNS resolution

kubectl patch serviceentry payment-ext -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/resolution","value":"DNS"}
]'
N4

🔴 NODE 4 — AuthorizationPolicy Blocking Egress

AuthZ Egress Rules

    
    
        
  • Check AuthorizationPolicies: kubectl get authorizationpolicy -A
    A DENY policy or restrictive ALLOW might block egress. Check if any policy has action: DENY with broad rules.
    • 
    




Allow egress to specific external host

kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata: {name: allow-payment-egress, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  action: ALLOW
  rules: [{to: [{operation: {hosts: ["api.payment-gateway.com"]}}]}]
EOF
DT8
🌳 DECISION TREE DT8 — AuthorizationPolicy Not Enforcing

ALLOW/DENY Policy Created But Traffic Not Blocked/Allowed

The Problem: You created an AuthorizationPolicy to restrict access to the anihpj-api — only the web frontend should call it. But unauthorized pods can STILL access the API. Or conversely: you created an ALLOW policy and now ALL traffic is blocked including legitimate requests. Istio RBAC is subtle — scope, principal format, and policy ordering all matter.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — AuthZ Policy Not Working as Expected

AuthZ Symptom

    
    
        
  • ALLOW policy created, but traffic still blocked?
    → DENY policy takes precedence, or principal/namespace wrong. Go to NODE 2
    • 
        
  • DENY/ALLOW policy created, but traffic NOT blocked?
    → Policy scope wrong, or no sidecar on workload. Go to NODE 3
    • 
        
  • Policy works for some pods but not others?
    → WorkloadSelector mismatch. Go to NODE 4
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — ALLOW Policy Not Working (Still Blocked)

ALLOW Policy Debug

    
    
        
  • Check SPIFFE principal format: istioctl proxy-config secret deploy/anihpj-web -n anihpj
    Principal MUST be: cluster.local/ns/anihpj/sa/anihpj-web-sa. Wrong format = no match.
    • 
        
  • DENY policy overriding? kubectl get authorizationpolicy -A -o yaml | grep "action: DENY"
    DENY always wins over ALLOW. Remove conflicting DENY policies.
    • 
    




Fix principal format in AuthZ policy

kubectl patch authorizationpolicy api-access -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/rules/0/from/0/source/principals","value":["cluster.local/ns/anihpj/sa/anihpj-web-sa"]}
]'
N3

🔴 NODE 3 — Policy Not Enforcing (Traffic Passes Through)

Enforcement Check

    
    
        
  • Target workload has sidecar?
    AuthZ is enforced by the DESTINATION's Envoy. Without a sidecar, no enforcement. Check: kubectl get pods -n anihpj — must be 2/2.
    • 
        
  • Policy in correct namespace?
    AuthZ policy applies to workloads in its OWN namespace. Policy in default doesn't protect anihpj.
    •
N4

🔴 NODE 4 — WorkloadSelector Mismatch

Selector Check

    
    
        
  • Check pod labels vs selector: kubectl get pods -n anihpj --show-labels vs kubectl get authorizationpolicy -o yaml | grep -A5 selector
    If no selector = applies to ALL workloads in namespace. If selector present, must match pod labels EXACTLY.
    •
DT9
🌳 DECISION TREE DT9 — Canary Traffic Split Not Working

Weight-Based Traffic Split Ignored — All Traffic Goes to One Version

The Problem: You configured a VirtualService with weight-based routing: 90% v1, 10% v2. But ALL traffic goes to v1. The canary deployment receives ZERO requests. Is it DestinationRule subsets? Weight totaling? Multiple VirtualServices conflicting? Follow this tree to get your canary working.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — Weight-Based Split Not Working

Traffic Split Diagnosis

    
    
        
  • Weights sum to 100? kubectl get vs -o yaml | grep weight
    Weights MUST total 100. 90+10=100 ✅. 80+10=90 ❌ — missing 10% goes to first route.
    • 
        
  • DestinationRule subsets defined?
    VS references subset: v2 but DR doesn't define v2? Subset not found = traffic falls back to Service default.
    • 
        
  • Multiple VS for same host? kubectl get vs -A | grep anihpj-api
    Istio merges VS for the same host. First VS's routes take priority over second.
    • 
    




Fix weights to total 100 and ensure subsets exist

kubectl patch vs anihpj-api-vs -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/http/0/route/0/weight","value":90},
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/http/0/route/1/weight","value":10}
]'
DT10
🌳 DECISION TREE DT10 — Gateway Not Receiving External Traffic

curl to External IP Fails — Gateway Not Routing Ingress Traffic

The Problem: You configured an Istio Gateway and VirtualService for external access. But curl http://jobpost.com fails — connection refused, timeout, or 404. The Gateway resource exists, the VirtualService is deployed, but traffic never reaches the backend. Is it the selector? Port mismatch? LoadBalancer pending?

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 1 (kubeadm)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — External Traffic Fails at Gateway

Gateway Ingress Failure — What's the Error?

    
    
        
  • Connection refused / no response
    → Gateway Service EXTERNAL-IP is Pending or wrong type. Go to NODE 2 (Service Type)
    • 
        
  • 404 Not Found
    → Gateway host or VirtualService host mismatch. Go to NODE 3 (Host Match)
    • 
        
  • 503 No Healthy Upstream
    → Gateway routes traffic but backend unreachable. Go to NODE 4 (Backend)
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — Gateway Service EXTERNAL-IP Pending

Service Type Check

    
    
        
  • kubectl get svc -n istio-system istio-ingressgateway
    Type: LoadBalancer on bare-metal? EXTERNAL-IP stays Pending forever. Change to NodePort or use MetalLB.
    • 
        
  • Gateway selector matches? kubectl get gateway -o yaml | grep selector vs kubectl get pods -n istio-system -l <selector>
    If no pods match the selector, Gateway has no Envoy to program.
    • 
    




Change to NodePort for bare-metal

kubectl patch svc istio-ingressgateway -n istio-system --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/type","value":"NodePort"}
]'
N3

🔴 NODE 3 — Host Mismatch Between Gateway and VirtualService

Host Alignment

    
    
        
  • Gateway hosts match VirtualService hosts?
    Gateway: hosts: ["jobpost.com"] but VS: hosts: ["www.jobpost.com"]? Must match EXACTLY. Check: kubectl get gateway,vs -n anihpj -o yaml | grep hosts
    • 
        
  • VS has gateways: field pointing to the Gateway?
    Without gateways: [gateway-name], VS is mesh-internal only — ignored by ingress.
    •
N4

🔴 NODE 4 — Backend Unreachable from Gateway

Backend Check

    
    
        
  • VS destination host matches Service?
    VS: host: anihpj-web but Service is anihpj-api? Host must match the Kubernetes Service name.
    • 
        
  • Gateway and backend in SAME namespace?
    Gateway only sees Services in its own namespace by default. For cross-namespace, the VS host must be fully qualified.
    •
DT11
🌳 DECISION TREE DT11 — Envoy Memory/CPU Pressure

istio-proxy OOMKilled or CPU Throttled — Sidecar Resource Exhaustion

The Problem: Envoy sidecars are crashing with OOMKilled, or pods are slow because istio-proxy is CPU throttled. As your mesh grows, every sidecar receives the FULL mesh configuration — 100s of VirtualServices, DestinationRules, and clusters. This exhausts Envoy's memory. Time to scope sidecars and tune resources.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — Sidecar OOMKilled or CPU Throttled

Resource Exhaustion — Check These

    
    
        
  • Check sidecar memory: kubectl top pods -n anihpj --containers | grep istio-proxy
    If >512MB: too many configs. Go to NODE 2 (Sidecar Scoping)
    • 
        
  • Check Envoy config size: istioctl proxy-config clusters deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj | wc -l
    Thousands of clusters? Each external ServiceEntry adds clusters. Use Sidecar resource to limit.
    • 
        
  • WASM plugins enabled?
    WASM plugins consume significant CPU. Check: kubectl get wasmplugin -A. Disable unused plugins.
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — Sidecar Resource Scoping

Scope Sidecar Config

    
    
        
  • Create Sidecar resource to limit scope: By default, every sidecar receives ALL mesh config. Limit to only what this workload needs.
    Create a Sidecar resource with workloadSelector and specific egress.hosts.
    • 
    




Limit sidecar scope + increase resources

kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: Sidecar
metadata: {name: anihpj-api-scope, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  workloadSelector: {labels: {app: anihpj-api}}
  egress: [{hosts: ["anihpj/*", "istio-system/*"]}]
EOF

kubectl patch deploy anihpj-api -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/1/resources/limits/memory","value":"512Mi"}
]'
DT12
🌳 DECISION TREE DT12 — Istio Upgrade Failed / Mesh in Broken State

After Upgrade — Mesh Features Broken, Sidecars STALE, CRDs Mismatched

The Problem: You upgraded Istio from 1.20 to 1.22 using canary upgrade. The new istiod is running, but half the proxies show STALE, VirtualServices aren't applied, and some workloads crash. Did you forget to restart the data plane? Are CRDs mismatched? Did you decommission the old revision too early? Follow this tree to recover.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 1 (kubeadm)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — Mesh Broken After Upgrade

Upgrade Failure Mode

    
    
        
  • Old proxies still connected to OLD istiod?
    → Namespace still has old revision label. Go to NODE 2 (Revision Label)
    • 
        
  • New proxies fail to start?
    → CRD version mismatch or webhook issue. Go to NODE 3 (CRDs)
    • 
        
  • Everything broken, need rollback?
    → Old revision decommissioned? Go to NODE 4 (Rollback)
    •
N2

🔴 NODE 2 — Namespace Revision Label Still Points to Old istiod

Revision Migration

    
    
        
  • Check namespace label: kubectl get ns anihpj --show-labels | grep istio.io/rev
    Still shows 1-20? Change to 1-22 and restart pods: kubectl label ns anihpj istio.io/rev=1-22 --overwrite && kubectl rollout restart deploy -n anihpj
    •
N3

🔴 NODE 3 — CRD Version Mismatch

CRD Compatibility

    
    
        
  • Check CRD versions: kubectl get crds | grep istio.io
    Upgraded control plane but not CRDs? Run: istioctl install --set revision=1-22 -y — this updates CRDs.
    • 
        
  • istioctl analyze: istioctl analyze -n anihpj
    Shows validation errors for new CRD fields not recognized by old webhook.
    •
N4

🔴 NODE 4 — Emergency Rollback

Rollback Steps

    
    
        
  • Old revision still running? kubectl get pods -n istio-system -l app=istiod
    If old istiod was decommissioned: REINSTALL it! istioctl install --set revision=1-20 -y. Then switch namespace label back.
    • 
        
  • Mark new revision as unhealthy, switch back: kubectl label ns anihpj istio.io/rev=1-20 --overwrite && kubectl rollout restart deploy -n anihpj
    • 
    




Emergency rollback to previous revision

istioctl install --set revision=1-20 --set profile=default -y
kubectl label ns anihpj istio.io/rev=1-20 --overwrite
kubectl rollout restart deploy -n anihpj
DT13
🌳 DECISION TREE DT13 — Circuit Breaker Ejected All Endpoints

All Pods Ejected — Complete Service Outage from Circuit Breaker

The Problem: The circuit breaker ejected ALL API pods. Every request returns 503. Pods are healthy but Envoy won't route to them. The outlier detection was configured too aggressively — consecutive5xxErrors: 1 and maxEjectionPercent: 100. A brief network hiccup triggered a cascading ejection of every pod. Follow this tree to diagnose and tune.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — All Pods Ejected, 503 From Service

Circuit Breaker — What's the Setting?

    
    
        
  • Check outlier detection: kubectl get dr -o yaml | grep -A10 outlierDetection
    consecutive5xxErrors: 1? Too aggressive! Production: 5+. baseEjectionTime: 5m? Too long! Use 30s.
    • 
        
  • maxEjectionPercent = 100?
    This allows ALL pods to be ejected simultaneously. Cap at 50% to keep at least half the pods receiving traffic.
    • 
        
  • Are pods ACTUALLY unhealthy?
    Check: kubectl get pods — Running and Ready? If yes, it's a FALSE POSITIVE ejection. Tune thresholds.
    • 
    




Fix outlier detection to production-safe values

kubectl patch dr anihpj-api-dr -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/trafficPolicy/outlierDetection/consecutive5xxErrors","value":5},
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/trafficPolicy/outlierDetection/baseEjectionTime","value":"30s"},
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/trafficPolicy/outlierDetection/maxEjectionPercent","value":50}
]'


⚠️ Never set maxEjectionPercent to 100 in production — a transient network blip can eject ALL pods, causing complete outage.
DT14
🌳 DECISION TREE DT14 — DNS Resolution Failure for ServiceEntry

External Service Unreachable — DNS Resolution for ServiceEntry Fails

The Problem: You created a ServiceEntry for an external service, but the sidecar can't resolve the hostname. curl returns "could not resolve host." The ServiceEntry exists but Envoy has no endpoints for the cluster. Is it the resolution mode? DNS server reachable? Host field misspelled?

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — DNS Fails for External Service

DNS Resolution Diagnosis

    
    
        
  • resolution: NONE (default)?
    With sidecar, NONE breaks DNS. Change to resolution: DNS so Istio resolves the hostname to IPs.
    • 
        
  • resolution: DNS but host misspelled?
    Check: kubectl get serviceentry -o yaml | grep hosts. Typos = DNS lookup fails.
    • 
        
  • CoreDNS working?
    Check: kubectl exec deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj -- nslookup api.payment-gateway.com. If CoreDNS fails, no DNS resolution possible.
    • 
        
  • External DNS blocked by firewall?
    Istio uses cluster DNS (CoreDNS) which forwards to upstream DNS. If upstream blocked, resolution fails.
    • 
    




Change to DNS resolution + verify hostname

kubectl patch serviceentry payment-ext -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/resolution","value":"DNS"},
  {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/hosts/0","value":"api.payment-gateway.com"}
]'
DT15
🌳 DECISION TREE DT15 — Complete Mesh Degradation (Multiple Symptoms)

Everything Broken Simultaneously — Systematic Triage for Mesh-Wide Outage

The Problem: Multiple symptoms appear simultaneously: 503s everywhere, mTLS failing, proxies STALE, Kiali blank, new pods not injected. This is a mesh-wide degradation — likely a single root cause cascading into multiple failures. Don't chase individual symptoms — find the root cause systematically. This is your "war room" decision tree.

🖥️ CLUSTER: ksw → 2 (kind-cka-lab)
▶

🚦 NODE 1 — Multiple Symptoms, Mesh-Wide Outage

Triage — Check These in ORDER

    
    
        
  • ① Check istiod FIRST: kubectl get pods -n istio-system -l app=istiod
    If NOT Running: ALL mesh features are controlled by istiod. Restart it, check logs, check resources.
    • 
        
  • ② Check cert expiry: istioctl proxy-config secret deploy/<pod> -n anihpj | grep EXPIRED
    All certs expired? CA cert expired? Restart istiod to force rotation. If CA expired >24h ago, you may need to reinstall.
    • 
        
  • ③ Check resource pressure: kubectl top nodes and kubectl top pods -n istio-system
    Nodes full? istiod OOM? Cluster at capacity?
    • 
        
  • ④ Check recent changes: kubectl get events -A --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -30
    Recent deployment? ConfigMap change? Upgrade attempt? Someone deleted a namespace?
    • 
        
  • ⑤ Run istioctl bug-report: istioctl bug-report
    Collects ALL mesh diagnostics into a tar.gz. Include this in your incident report.
    • 
    




Emergency mesh recovery — restart control plane + data plane

kubectl rollout restart deploy/istiod -n istio-system
kubectl rollout restart deploy -n anihpj
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pods --all -n anihpj --timeout=120s
istioctl proxy-status


⚠️ WAR ROOM RULE: When everything is broken, fix istiod first. Without a healthy control plane, nothing else matters. Then check certs. Then check resources. NEVER start debugging individual VirtualServices until the control plane is confirmed healthy.

📊 Scoring Guide — How To Use This Answer Key

❌ Below 70% — Foundation Needed

Focus on the Pre-Learning section (F.1–F.5) and Category 1–2 MCQs. Build your mental model before attempting scenarios.

⚠️ 70–84% — Practice Needed

You have the fundamentals. Focus on Part 2 Issues and Part 3 Scenarios to build diagnostic muscle memory.

✅ 85–94% — Exam Ready

Strong foundation. Review Decision Trees and Appendix C (20 Exam Command Patterns) for exam day.

🚀 95%+ — Service Mesh Expert

You've mastered Istio. Time to explore Beyond Istio (Appendix K) and platform engineering patterns.

📚 Appendix B: Top 100 Istio/Envoy CommandsTOOLKIT

🛠️ Your Daily Istio & Envoy Command Toolkit

Master these 100 commands to debug, configure, and operate your Istio service mesh. Organized by operational category. Every command is copy-paste ready with real anihpj namespace examples. Muscle memory for the ICA exam: type these from memory.

📦 1. Installation & Upgrade (12 Commands)

#CommandPurpose
1istioctl install --set profile=demo -yInstall Istio with demo profile (all components)
2istioctl install --set profile=default -yInstall with default profile (istiod + ingress only)
3istioctl install --set profile=ambient -yInstall ambient mesh (ztunnel + waypoint)
4istioctl install --set revision=1-22 --set profile=default -yCanary: install new istiod revision
5istioctl upgradeIn-place upgrade (not recommended for production)

8istioctl operator initInitialize Istio operator for declarative management

📚 Appendix C: 20 Exam Day Command Patterns ⚡CRAM

⚡ Last-30-Minute Cram Sheet — 20 Command Patterns You MUST Know

These 20 patterns cover 90% of ICA exam tasks. Read this 30 minutes before your exam. Type M.1, M.2, M.6, and M.10 from memory. Every pattern is a complete, self-contained command sequence — copy-paste, adapt the namespace, and execute. This is your exam-day lifeline.

⚡ M.1 — Install Istio

When: "Install Istio on this cluster" task. 5 seconds.
istioctl install --set profile=demo -y
kubectl label ns default istio-injection=enabled

⚡ M.2 — Enable Sidecar Injection

When: Pods show 1/1 instead of 2/2. 15 seconds.
kubectl label ns anihpj istio-injection=enabled --overwrite
kubectl rollout restart deploy -n anihpj
kubectl get pods -n anihpj  # should be 2/2

⚡ M.3 — Check Proxy Sync Status

When: "Are all proxies SYNCED?" 3 seconds.
istioctl proxy-status
# ALL must show SYNCED for CDS, LDS, EDS, RDS

⚡ M.4 — Dump Envoy Route Config

When: "Why is traffic going to the wrong service?" 10 seconds.
istioctl proxy-config routes deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj
istioctl proxy-config clusters deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj

⚡ M.5 — Debug mTLS Certificates

When: "mTLS handshake fails." 10 seconds.
istioctl proxy-config secret deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj
# Check for EXPIRED or VALIDATION ERROR

⚡ M.6 — Test Authorization Policy

When: "Will this principal be allowed?" 15 seconds.
istioctl x authz check deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj \
  --principal "cluster.local/ns/anihpj/sa/web-sa"

⚡ M.7 — Analyze Istio Configuration

When: "Find all config errors." 5 seconds.
istioctl analyze -n anihpj
istioctl analyze -A  # all namespaces

⚡ M.8 — Canary Deployment

When: "Route 90% v1, 10% v2." 30 seconds.
kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata: {name: api-vs, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  hosts: [anihpj-api]
  http:
  - route:
    - destination: {host: anihpj-api, subset: v1}
      weight: 90
    - destination: {host: anihpj-api, subset: v2}
      weight: 10
EOF

⚡ M.9 — Enable mTLS STRICT Mesh-Wide

When: "Enforce mTLS across entire mesh." 10 seconds.
kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata: {name: default, namespace: istio-system}
spec: {mtls: {mode: STRICT}}
EOF

⚡ M.10 — ALLOW AuthZ by SPIFFE Principal

When: "Only web-sa can call api." 20 seconds.
kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata: {name: api-access, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["cluster.local/ns/anihpj/sa/anihpj-web-sa"]
EOF

⚡ M.11 — Check Certificate Expiry

When: "Are mesh certs expiring?" 15 seconds.
istioctl proxy-config secret deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj \
  -o json | jq -r '.dynamicActiveSecrets[0].secret.tlsCertificate.certificateChain.inlineBytes' | base64 -d | openssl x509 -noout -dates

⚡ M.12 — Gateway with TLS (HTTPS)

When: "Expose service on HTTPS." 25 seconds.
kubectl create secret tls jobpost-tls-secret \
  --cert=jobpost.crt --key=jobpost.key -n anihpj
kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: Gateway
metadata: {name: anihpj-gateway, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  selector: {istio: ingressgateway}
  servers:
  - port: {number: 443, name: https, protocol: HTTPS}
    hosts: ["jobpost.com"]
    tls: {mode: SIMPLE, credentialName: jobpost-tls-secret}
EOF

⚡ M.13 — ServiceEntry for External Service

When: "Allow egress to external API." 15 seconds.
kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata: {name: payment-ext, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  hosts: [api.payment-gateway.com]
  ports: [{number: 443, name: https, protocol: HTTPS}]
  resolution: DNS
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL
EOF

⚡ M.14 — Circuit Breaker (Outlier Detection)

When: "Eject unhealthy pods." 20 seconds.
kubectl patch dr anihpj-api-dr -n anihpj --type=json -p='[
  {"op":"add","path":"/spec/trafficPolicy/outlierDetection",
   "value":{consecutive5xxErrors:5,interval:"10s",
            baseEjectionTime:"30s",maxEjectionPercent:50}}
]'

⚡ M.15 — Fault Injection (Delay/Abort)

When: "Inject 5s delay on 50% of traffic." 15 seconds.
kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata: {name: api-fault, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  hosts: [anihpj-api]
  http:
  - fault:
      delay: {percentage: {value: 50}, fixedDelay: 5s}
    route:
    - destination: {host: anihpj-api}
EOF

⚡ M.16 — Traffic Mirroring (Dark Launch)

When: "Mirror 100% traffic to v2 for testing." 15 seconds.
kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata: {name: api-mirror, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  hosts: [anihpj-api]
  http:
  - route: [{destination: {host: anihpj-api, subset: v1}}]
    mirror:
      host: anihpj-api
      subset: v2
EOF

⚡ M.17 — Open Kiali Dashboard

When: "Visualize the service mesh graph." 3 seconds.
istioctl dashboard kiali

⚡ M.18 — Open Jaeger Tracing

When: "Trace a request through the mesh." 3 seconds.
istioctl dashboard jaeger

⚡ M.19 — Get Envoy Access Logs

When: "See what requests Envoy is handling." 5 seconds.
kubectl logs deploy/anihpj-api -n anihpj -c istio-proxy --tail=100

⚡ M.20 — Collect All Diagnostics

When: "Everything is broken — collect everything for support." 30 seconds.

📚 Appendix D: YAML Reference TemplatesTEMPLATES

📋 Every Istio Resource — Complete Copy-Paste YAML Templates

All 12 Istio CRD templates with every required field + commonly used optional fields. Each template uses real anihpj/jobpost values, annotated with comments explaining what each section does. Copy, paste, adapt the namespace and host values — deploy instantly.

🚦 1. VirtualService — HTTP Routing, Canary, Mirror, Fault Injection

YAML — VirtualService: Canary 90/10 + /test → v3 + Mirror + Fault Injection 
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: anihpj-api-vs        # Unique name in namespace
  namespace: anihpj           # Must match Gateway namespace (for ingress)
spec:
  hosts:
  - anihpj-api               # Short name OR FQDN: anihpj-api.anihpj.svc.cluster.local
  gateways:                  # Omit for mesh-internal; include for ingress gateway
  - anihpj-gateway           # Gateway name this VS binds to
  http:                      # HTTP routing rules (evaluated in ORDER — first match wins!)
  # Rule 1: Route /test prefix → subset v3 (experimental)
  - match:
    - uri:
        prefix: /test         # Options: prefix, exact, regex
    route:
    - destination:
        host: anihpj-api     # Destination service name
        subset: v3            # DestinationRule subset (must exist!)
        port:
          number: 8080
  # Rule 2: Canary split — 90% v1, 10% v2
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: anihpj-api
        subset: v1
      weight: 90              # ALL weights must total 100
    - destination:
        host: anihpj-api
        subset: v2
      weight: 10
  # Rule 3: Redirect HTTP → HTTPS
  - match:
    - uri:
        prefix: /admin
    redirect:                 # 301/302 redirect (not rewrite)
      uri: https://admin.jobpost.com/
      authority: admin.jobpost.com
      redirectCode: 301
  # Rule 4: Mirror 100% traffic to v2 (dark launch)
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: anihpj-api
        subset: v1
      weight: 100
    mirror:                   # Send copy to v2 — v1 handles response
      host: anihpj-api
      subset: v2
  # Rule 5: Fault injection — 50% delay, 10% 500 abort
  - fault:
      delay:                  # Inject artificial latency
        percentage:
          value: 50
        fixedDelay: 5s
      abort:                  # Inject HTTP 500 errors
        percentage:
          value: 10
        httpStatus: 500
    route:
    - destination:
        host: anihpj-api
        subset: v1
  # Rule 6: Timeout + Retries
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: anihpj-api
      weight: 100
    timeout: 10s              # Request timeout
    retries:                  # Retry on 5xx, reset, connect-failure
      attempts: 3
      perTryTimeout: 2s
      retryOn: "5xx,reset,connect-failure"
  # CORS policy (browser-based APIs)
  - corsPolicy:
      allowOrigins:
      - exact: "https://jobpost.com"
      allowMethods: ["GET","POST","PUT","DELETE"]
      allowHeaders: ["Authorization","Content-Type"]
      maxAge: "24h"
    route:
    - destination:
        host: anihpj-api

🎯 2. DestinationRule — Subsets, LB, Connection Pool, Outlier Detection

YAML — DestinationRule: Subsets + ROUND_ROBIN + Connection Pool + Circuit Breaker 
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: anihpj-api-dr
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  host: anihpj-api           # Service name — must match Service exactly
  subsets:                   # Named groups of pods identified by labels
  - name: v1                 # Stable version
    labels:
      app-version: v1         # MUST match pod labels EXACTLY (key + value)
    trafficPolicy:            # Per-subset policy (only applies when THIS subset is used)
      loadBalancer:
        simple: LEAST_REQUEST # LB for this subset only
  - name: v2                 # Canary version
    labels:
      app-version: v2
  - name: v3                 # Experimental version
    labels:
      app-version: v3
  trafficPolicy:             # TOP-LEVEL policy — applies to ALL routes
    loadBalancer:
      # Options: ROUND_ROBIN, LEAST_REQUEST, RANDOM, PASSTHROUGH
      simple: ROUND_ROBIN
      # Consistent hash for session affinity (MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with 'simple')
      # consistentHash:
      #   httpHeaderName: "X-User-ID"  # Hash based on HTTP header
      #   httpCookie:
      #     name: "session-id"         # Hash based on cookie
      #     ttl: 3600s
    connectionPool:           # Connection pool limits
      tcp:
        maxConnections: 100    # Max simultaneous TCP connections
        connectTimeout: 10s    # TCP connection timeout
      http:
        http1MaxPendingRequests: 50  # Queue for HTTP/1.1 pending requests
        http2MaxRequests: 1000       # Max concurrent HTTP/2 requests
        maxRequestsPerConnection: 0  # 0 = unlimited (HTTP/1.1 keep-alive)
        maxRetries: 3                # Max retry attempts
        idleTimeout: 1h              # Idle connection timeout
    outlierDetection:         # Circuit breaker — eject unhealthy pods
      consecutive5xxErrors: 5 # Errors before ejection (production: 5+)
      interval: 10s           # Evaluation interval
      baseEjectionTime: 30s   # Minimum ejection duration
      maxEjectionPercent: 50  # Cap: NEVER set to 100 in production!
      consecutiveGatewayErrors: 3  # Gateway-specific error threshold
    tls:                      # TLS settings for this destination
      mode: ISTIO_MUTUAL      # DISABLE | SIMPLE | MUTUAL | ISTIO_MUTUAL
      # caCertificates: /etc/certs/root-ca.pem  # Custom CA cert

🚪 3. Gateway — Ingress, Egress, TLS PASSTHROUGH/SIMPLE/MUTUAL

YAML — Gateway: HTTP(80) + HTTPS(443) + TCP(5432) + TLS PASSTHROUGH 
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: anihpj-gateway
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:                  # Pod labels of the gateway proxy
    istio: ingressgateway    # Default istio-ingressgateway pod label
  servers:                   # List of L4-L6 listeners
  # Server 1: HTTP port 80 — redirect to HTTPS
  - port:
      number: 80
      name: http
      protocol: HTTP          # HTTP | HTTPS | TLS | TCP | gRPC
    hosts:
    - "jobpost.com"          # SNI hostname (use * for wildcard)
  # Server 2: HTTPS port 443 — TLS SIMPLE (server-side TLS)
  - port:
      number: 443
      name: https
      protocol: HTTPS
    hosts:
    - "jobpost.com"
    tls:
      mode: SIMPLE            # Server TLS — Gateway terminates TLS
      credentialName: jobpost-tls-secret  # Kubernetes TLS Secret name
  # Server 3: HTTPS port 443 — TLS MUTUAL (mTLS at edge)
  # tls:
  #   mode: MUTUAL             # Both client AND server certs
  #   credentialName: jobpost-mtls-secret
  # Server 4: TLS PASSTHROUGH — SNI-based routing (no decryption)
  - port:
      number: 443
      name: tls-passthrough
      protocol: TLS           # TLS protocol (not HTTPS)
    hosts:
    - "api.jobpost.com"      # SPECIFIC: never use * on multiple PASSTHROUGH servers!
    tls:
      mode: PASSTHROUGH       # Forward raw TLS to backend
  # Server 5: TCP port 5432 — PostgreSQL passthrough
  - port:
      number: 5432
      name: tcp-postgres
      protocol: TCP
    hosts:
    - "db.jobpost.internal"

🌐 4. ServiceEntry — External Service Registration (STATIC / DNS)

YAML — ServiceEntry: DNS resolution + STATIC IP endpoint 
# Template 1: DNS resolution for external API
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata:
  name: payment-gateway-ext
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  hosts:
  - api.payment-gateway.com  # External hostname (supports *.example.com wildcard)
  ports:
  - number: 443
    name: https
    protocol: HTTPS
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL      # MESH_EXTERNAL | MESH_INTERNAL
  resolution: DNS             # NONE (default, breaks with sidecar) | STATIC | DNS
---
# Template 2: STATIC IP for external database
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata:
  name: external-postgres
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  hosts:
  - external-db.example.com
  addresses:                  # STATIC: hardcoded IPs
  - 192.168.1.100
  - 192.168.1.101
  ports:
  - number: 5432
    name: tcp-postgres
    protocol: TCP
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL
  resolution: STATIC
  endpoints:                  # Manual endpoint definition
  - address: 192.168.1.100
    ports:
      tcp-postgres: 5432
  - address: 192.168.1.101
    ports:
      tcp-postgres: 5432
  exportTo:                   # Visibility: * (all), . (none), specific namespace
  - "*"

🔐 5. PeerAuthentication — mTLS (Mesh-Wide, Namespace, Workload)

YAML — PeerAuthentication: Mesh STRICT + Namespace PERMISSIVE + Workload STRICT 
# Template 1: Mesh-wide STRICT mTLS (all namespaces)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: istio-system     # MUST be in istio-system for mesh-wide
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT              # STRICT | PERMISSIVE | DISABLE
---
# Template 2: Namespace-level PERMISSIVE (overrides mesh-wide)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: anihpj           # Applied to THIS namespace only
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: PERMISSIVE          # Allows both mTLS and plaintext
---
# Template 3: Workload-level STRICT (specific deployment)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: db-strict
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:                   # Workload selector — targets specific pods
    matchLabels:
      app: anihpj-db
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT              # Only this workload enforces STRICT
---
# Template 4: Port-level mTLS exclusion
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: exclude-health-port
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: anihpj-api
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
  portLevelMtls:              # Per-port mTLS override
    9090:
      mode: PERMISSIVE        # Port 9090 excluded from STRICT

🎫 6. RequestAuthentication — JWT Validation

YAML — RequestAuthentication: JWT with JWKS URI + Audiences 
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: RequestAuthentication
metadata:
  name: jwt-auth
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:                   # Optional — applies to all workloads in ns if omitted
    matchLabels:
      app: anihpj-api
  jwtRules:
  - issuer: "https://auth.example.com"  # MUST match token 'iss' claim EXACTLY
    jwksUri: "https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json"  # JWKS endpoint
    audiences:                 # Token 'aud' must match one of these
    - "anihpj-api"
    - "anihpj-web"
    fromHeaders:               # Which header(s) contain the JWT
    - name: Authorization
      prefix: "Bearer "       # Strip this prefix before validation
    forwardOriginalToken: true # Forward original JWT to backend
    outputPayloadToHeader: "X-JWT-Payload"  # Write decoded payload to header
  # Multiple JWT issuers (validate against ANY of these)
  - issuer: "https://auth2.example.com"
    jwksUri: "https://auth2.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json"

🛡️ 7. AuthorizationPolicy — ALLOW, DENY, CUSTOM

YAML — AuthorizationPolicy: ALLOW by principal + DENY by IP + path/method restrictions 
# Template 1: ALLOW — only web service account can call API
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: api-access
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  action: ALLOW              # ALLOW | DENY | CUSTOM
  selector:                   # Target workload (omit for all in namespace)
    matchLabels:
      app: anihpj-api
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals:           # SPIFFE identity format
        - "cluster.local/ns/anihpj/sa/anihpj-web-sa"
        namespaces:            # All workloads from this namespace
        - "anihpj"
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET","POST"]  # Only allow GET and POST
        paths: ["/api/*"]        # Only allow /api/* paths
    when:                      # Additional conditions
    - key: request.auth.claims[group]
      values: ["admin","editor"]
---
# Template 2: DENY — block specific IP range
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-external-ips
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  action: DENY               # DENY takes precedence over ALLOW!
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        ipBlocks:
        - "192.168.0.0/16"   # Block this IP range
---
# Template 3: Default deny + specific allow (least privilege)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: anihpj
spec: {}                      # Empty rules = DENY ALL (no selector = all workloads)

🔌 8. EnvoyFilter — HTTP Filter, Network Filter

YAML — EnvoyFilter: Add custom HTTP header + Network filter 
# Template 1: HTTP filter — add custom header to all responses
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: add-custom-header
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      app: anihpj-api
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER       # LISTENER | NETWORK_FILTER | HTTP_FILTER | ROUTE_CONFIGURATION
    match:
      context: SIDECAR_OUTBOUND
      listener:
        filterChain:
          filter:
            name: "envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager"
            subFilter:
              name: "envoy.filters.http.router"
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_BEFORE
      value:
        name: "envoy.filters.http.lua"
        typed_config:
          "@type": "type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua"
          inlineCode: |
            function envoy_on_response(response_handle)
              response_handle:headers():add("X-Mesh", "istio")
              response_handle:headers():add("X-Pod", os.getenv("HOSTNAME"))
            end
---
# Template 2: Network filter — rate limiting (simplified)
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: rate-limit
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      app: anihpj-api
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: NETWORK_FILTER
    match:
      context: SIDECAR_INBOUND
      listener:
        portNumber: 8080
        filterChain:
          filter:
            name: "envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager"
    patch:
      operation: MERGE
      value:
        typed_config:
          "@type": "type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager"
          route_config:
            virtual_hosts:
            - name: local_route
              domains: ["*"]
              routes:
              - match:
                  prefix: "/"
                route:
                  cluster: "inbound|8080||"
              rate_limits:
              - actions:
                - remote_address: {}

📐 9. Sidecar — Scope Limiting (Reduce Memory)

YAML — Sidecar: Limit egress hosts + ingress listeners 
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: Sidecar
metadata:
  name: anihpj-api-scope
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  workloadSelector:           # Which workloads this applies to
    labels:
      app: anihpj-api
  egress:                     # Limit what hosts the sidecar can reach
  - hosts:
    - "anihpj/*"              # All services in anihpj namespace
    - "istio-system/*"        # istiod + observability components
    # - "./*"                 # All services in current namespace
    # - "*/anihpj-web.anihpj.svc.cluster.local"  # Specific service FQDN
  ingress:                    # Limit what can reach this workload
  - port:
      number: 8080
      protocol: HTTP
      name: http
    defaultEndpoint: 127.0.0.1:8080

📊 10. Telemetry — Metrics Override + Access Logging

YAML — Telemetry: Custom metrics tags + enable access logging 
apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1alpha1
kind: Telemetry
metadata:
  name: anihpj-mesh-telemetry
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:                   # Target workloads (omit for namespace-wide)
    matchLabels:
      app: anihpj-api
  metrics:                    # Metrics customization
  - providers:
    - name: prometheus
    overrides:                # Add/remove/override metric tags
    - match:
        metric: REQUEST_COUNT
        mode: CLIENT
      tagOverrides:
        destination_port:
          value: "string(destination.port)"
        request_path:
          value: "request.url_path"
    - match:
        metric: REQUEST_DURATION
      tagOverrides:
        response_code:
          value: "response.code"
  accessLogging:              # Enable/configure access logs
  - providers:
    - name: envoy
    match:
      mode: CLIENT_AND_SERVER
    filter:                   # Only log 5xx responses
      expression: "response.code >= 500"

🧩 11. WasmPlugin — WebAssembly Extensions

YAML — WasmPlugin: Custom HTTP filter via WebAssembly 
apiVersion: extensions.istio.io/v1alpha1
kind: WasmPlugin
metadata:
  name: custom-rate-limit
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: anihpj-api
  url: oci://ghcr.io/anihpj/rate-limit-wasm:v1.0.0  # WASM binary URL
  # OR use local file:
  # url: file:///etc/istio/wasm/rate-limit.wasm
  imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  phase: AUTHZ               # Filter phase: AUTHN | AUTHZ | STATS
  pluginConfig:               # Plugin-specific configuration (JSON)
    rate: 100
    burst: 50
    perSecond: true

⚙️ 12. IstioOperator — Declarative Installation

YAML — IstioOperator: Full declarative mesh configuration 
apiVersion: install.istio.io/v1alpha1
kind: IstioOperator
metadata:
  name: anihpj-istio-config
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  profile: default            # demo | default | minimal | ambient | empty
  revision: 1-22              # Revision label for canary upgrades
  components:
    pilot:
      k8s:
        resources:
          requests: {cpu: 500m, memory: 2048Mi}
          limits: {cpu: 2000m, memory: 4096Mi}
        hpaSpec:              # Autoscaling for istiod
          minReplicas: 2
          maxReplicas: 5
    ingressGateways:
    - name: istio-ingressgateway
      k8s:
        service:
          type: NodePort       # LoadBalancer (cloud) | NodePort (bare-metal)
        resources:
          requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi}
    egressGateways:
    - name: istio-egressgateway
      enabled: true            # Enable egress gateway
  meshConfig:
    accessLogFile: /dev/stdout # Enable Envoy access logging
    accessLogFormat: |
      [%START_TIME%] "%REQ(:METHOD)% %REQ(X-ENVOY-ORIGINAL-PATH?:PATH)% %PROTOCOL%" %RESPONSE_CODE% %RESPONSE_FLAGS% %BYTES_RECEIVED% %BYTES_SENT% %DURATION% "%REQ(X-FORWARDED-FOR)%" "%REQ(USER-AGENT)%" "%REQ(X-REQUEST-ID)%" "%REQ(:AUTHORITY)%" "%UPSTREAM_HOST%"
    enableTracing: true
    defaultConfig:
      proxyMetadata:
        ISTIO_META_DNS_CAPTURE: "true"   # DNS proxying
  values:
    global:
      proxy:
        resources:
          requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi}
          limits: {cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi}
