🐳 Dockerfile — Multi-Stage, Non-Root, Distroless

Dockerfile — python:3.12-slim → gcr.io/distroless/python3 
# Stage 1: Build — compile dependencies
FROM python:3.12-slim AS builder
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --user poetry
COPY pyproject.toml poetry.lock ./
RUN poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes > requirements.txt
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --user -r requirements.txt

# Stage 2: Production — minimal, non-root, distroless
FROM gcr.io/distroless/python3-debian12
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /root/.local /root/.local
COPY . /app/
# Create non-root user (distroless runs as non-root by default)
USER 1000:1000
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:$PATH" \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=anihpj.settings
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["gunicorn", "anihpj.wsgi:application", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8080", "--workers", "4", "--timeout", "120"]

🐳 docker-compose.yml — Local Development

docker-compose.yml — Local dev: web + db + redis + celery 
version: "3.9"
services:
  web:
    build: .
    ports: ["8000:8080"]
    environment:
      - DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=anihpj.settings
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://anihpj:secret123@db:5432/jobpost
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
    depends_on: [db, redis]
    volumes: ["./anihpj:/app/anihpj", "./jobpost:/app/jobpost"]

  api:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports: ["8001:8080"]
    environment:
      - DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=anihpj.settings
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://anihpj:secret123@db:5432/jobpost
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
    depends_on: [db, redis]

  celery:
    build: .
    command: celery -A anihpj worker -l INFO
    environment:
      - DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=anihpj.settings
      - CELERY_BROKER_URL=redis://redis:6379/1
    depends_on: [db, redis]

  db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: anihpj
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret123
      POSTGRES_DB: jobpost
    ports: ["5432:5432"]
    volumes: ["pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data"]

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports: ["6379:6379"]

volumes:
  pgdata:

📚 Appendix F: Architecture & Attack SurfaceSECURITY

🛡️ Istio Service Mesh — Security Architecture & Attack Surface Analysis

Understanding the Istio security architecture is critical for the ICA exam and real-world mesh operations. This appendix maps the complete attack surface, security boundaries, threat vectors, and defense-in-depth layers that Istio provides. Know your enemy — and know your defenses.

🏰 Defense-in-Depth — Istio Security Layers

Istio Security Architecture — 7 Layers of Defense
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                     🛡️ LAYER 1: EDGE SECURITY                        │
  │  • Gateway TLS (SIMPLE/MUTUAL/PASSTHROUGH)                          │
  │  • Ingress AuthorizationPolicy (JWT validation at edge)             │
  │  • Rate limiting via EnvoyFilter                                    │
  │  • WAF integration via WASM plugins                                  │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │                     🔐 LAYER 2: TRANSPORT SECURITY (mTLS)            │
  │  • PeerAuthentication — mesh-wide / namespace / workload STRICT     │
  │  • Automatic mTLS between all sidecars                              │
  │  • SPIFFE identity: spiffe://cluster.local/ns/<ns>/sa/<sa>         │
  │  • Certificate rotation every 24h (auto-managed by istiod)          │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │                     🎫 LAYER 3: AUTHENTICATION (AuthN)               │
  │  • RequestAuthentication — JWT / OAuth2 / OIDC                      │
  │  • JWKS-based token validation                                      │
  │  • Multiple issuers supported                                        │
  │  • Token forwarding + payload-to-header output                       │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │                     🚦 LAYER 4: AUTHORIZATION (AuthZ)                │
  │  • AuthorizationPolicy — ALLOW / DENY / CUSTOM                      │
  │  • Source: principal, namespace, IP block                            │
  │  • Operation: method, path, host, port                               │
  │  • Conditions: JWT claims, headers                                   │
  │  • External authorization (extAuthz gRPC/HTTP)                       │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │                     📊 LAYER 5: OBSERVABILITY (Detection)            │
  │  • Envoy access logs — every request logged                          │
  │  • Prometheus metrics — request rates, errors, latencies            │
  │  • Kiali graph — visualize traffic flows + security status           │
  │  • Jaeger traces — trace individual requests across services        │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │                     🌐 LAYER 6: EGRESS CONTROL                       │
  │  • Egress Gateway — all outbound traffic audited                    │
  │  • ServiceEntry — explicit allow-list for external services          │
  │  • TLS origination — encrypt traffic to external services            │
  │  • DNS resolution control — ISTIO_META_DNS_CAPTURE                   │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │                     ⚙️ LAYER 7: PLATFORM HARDENING                   │
  │  • Pod Security Standards — non-root, read-only filesystem           │
  │  • NetworkPolicy — defense outside the mesh                          │
  │  • RBAC — Kubernetes-level access control for Istio CRDs            │
  │  • IstioOperator — declarative, auditable configuration              │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

🎯 Attack Surface — Entry Points

#Attack VectorIstio Defense
1External HTTP/HTTPS — ingress gatewayGateway TLS + AuthZ at edge + JWT validation
2mTLS bypass — plaintext injectionPeerAuthentication STRICT + sidecar enforcement
3JWT token theft/replayShort-lived tokens + JWKS rotation + audience validation
4RBAC escalation — pod label spoofingSPIFFE identity (cryptographic, not label-based)
5Sidecar bypass — direct pod IP accessNetworkPolicy + iptables REDIRECT (all traffic→Envoy)
6Egress data exfiltrationEgress Gateway + ServiceEntry allow-list + TLS origination
7istiod compromise — CA key theftRBAC for istiod + namespace isolation + audit logging
8Envoy config poisoning — malicious CRDistioctl analyze + admission webhook validation + RBAC

⚠️ Common Misconfigurations

#MisconfigurationImpact
1PERMISSIVE mTLS in productionAttackers can send plaintext, bypassing encryption
2AuthorizationPolicy too broadUnintended services can access sensitive APIs
3Gateway hosts: ["*"]Any hostname accepted → SNI spoofing
4ServiceEntry resolution: NONEDNS leaks through sidecar, bypassing egress control
5No AuthZ on ingress gatewayUnauthenticated requests reach backend services
6JWT without audience checkToken from one service accepted by another
7outboundTrafficPolicy: ALLOW_ANYAny egress allowed — data exfiltration possible
8No Sidecar resource scopingSidecar sees entire mesh → amplified blast radius

✅ Security Checklist — Production Hardening

🔒 Production Security Requirements (ICA Exam Focus)
  • ① mTLS: STRICT mesh-wide PeerAuthentication in istio-system
    kubectl apply -f peerauthentication-strict.yaml — All pod-to-pod traffic encrypted with auto-rotated SPIFFE certs.
  • ② Gateway TLS: SIMPLE (server) or MUTUAL (mTLS) for all ingress
    kubectl create secret tls <name> --cert=cert.pem --key=key.pem -n <ns>
  • ③ AuthorizationPolicy: default-deny + specific ALLOW rules
    Apply empty AuthZ policy to deny all, then add ALLOW policies for each legitimate traffic path.
  • ④ JWT validation: RequestAuthentication on all /api/* endpoints
    Validate iss, aud, exp claims. Use short-lived tokens with refresh.
  • ⑤ Egress control: ServiceEntry allow-list + Egress Gateway
    Set outboundTrafficPolicy.mode: REGISTRY_ONLY in MeshConfig.
  • ⑥ Sidecar scoping: limit egress hosts to reduce blast radius
    Create Sidecar resource with specific egress.hosts for each workload.
  • ⑦ Observability: Enable access logs + metrics + tracing
    meshConfig.accessLogFile: /dev/stdout + Prometheus ServiceMonitors.
  • ⑧ Regular auditing: istioctl analyze + istioctl proxy-status
    Run istioctl analyze -A to catch configuration drift and security gaps.

⚡ NLB + Istio Gateway

apiVersion: install.istio.io/v1alpha1
kind: IstioOperator
spec:
  components:
    ingressGateways:
    - name: istio-ingressgateway
      k8s:
        serviceAnnotations:
          # NLB instead of classic ELB
          service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: nlb
          # Enable proxy protocol for real client IP
          service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-proxy-protocol: "*"
          # Cross-zone load balancing
          service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-cross-zone-load-balancing-enabled: "true"
          # ACM certificate ARN
          service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-cert: "arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:123456:certificate/abc-123"
          # TLS termination at NLB
          service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-ports: "443"
          # Backend protocol (TCP to Envoy)
          service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: tcp

🔐 ACM Certificate + cert-manager

# cert-manager ClusterIssuer for Let's Encrypt
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata: {name: letsencrypt-prod}
spec:
  acme:
    server: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
    email: ops@anihpj.com
    privateKeySecretRef: {name: letsencrypt-prod}
    solvers:
    - http01:
        ingress:
          class: istio  # Route challenge through Istio
---
# Certificate for Gateway TLS
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata: {name: jobpost-tls, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  secretName: jobpost-tls-secret
  dnsNames: ["jobpost.com","*.jobpost.com"]
  issuerRef: {name: letsencrypt-prod, kind: ClusterIssuer}

🪪 IRSA — IAM Roles for Service Accounts

# 1. Create IAM OIDC provider for EKS
eksctl utils associate-iam-oidc-provider \
  --cluster anihpj-eks --approve

# 2. Create IAM role + policy for S3 access
eksctl create iamserviceaccount \
  --name anihpj-api-sa \
  --namespace anihpj \
  --cluster anihpj-eks \
  --attach-policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonS3FullAccess \
  --approve

# 3. Use the service account in Deployment
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: anihpj-api-sa
  namespace: anihpj
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "arn:aws:iam::123456:role/anihpj-api-s3"

🌐 ServiceEntry for AWS Services

# S3 — via VPC Endpoint (private IP)
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata: {name: aws-s3, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  hosts: [s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com]
  ports: [{number: 443, name: https, protocol: HTTPS}]
  resolution: DNS
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL
---
# DynamoDB — via VPC Endpoint
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata: {name: aws-dynamodb, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  hosts: [dynamodb.us-east-1.amazonaws.com]
  ports: [{number: 443, name: https, protocol: HTTPS}]
  resolution: DNS
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL
---
# RDS PostgreSQL — STATIC resolution
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata: {name: aws-rds, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  hosts: [anihpj-db.xyz.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com]
  addresses: [10.0.1.50]
  ports: [{number: 5432, name: tcp, protocol: TCP}]
  resolution: STATIC
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL

🎯 ICA Exam Day — Your Complete Battle Plan

The CNCF Istio Certified Administrator (ICA) exam is a 2-hour, performance-based, hands-on exam. You'll be given a Kubernetes cluster with Istio pre-installed and a set of tasks. This guide covers everything: preparation checklist, environment setup, time management, task triage, common pitfalls, and recovery procedures. Read this the morning of your exam.

✅ Pre-Exam Checklist (Day Before)

24 Hours Before — Must Complete
  • Test your environment: Open the PSI browser, run the system check. Camera, microphone, screen sharing must work. Do this NOW, not 10 minutes before.
  • Clear your desk: Papers, books, phones, second monitors — ALL must be removed. Water in a clear glass is allowed.
  • Read the Candidate Handbook: Know the rules. No bathroom breaks (plan accordingly). No eating. No talking.
  • Charge your laptop: Plugged in during exam. Close ALL other applications (Slack, email, browsers).
  • Review Appendix C (20 Command Patterns): Type M.1-M.5 from memory. These are your lifeline.
  • Sleep 8 hours: Cramming the night before does more harm than good. Trust your preparation.

⏰ Time Management — The 7-Minute Rule

Time LeftTasks DoneStrategy
120 min0Setup (5 min): aliases, verify context, scan all tasks, create notes file
115 min0Easy tasks first: Build confidence. "Label a namespace." "Check proxy-status."
85 min~5Medium tasks: "Create a VirtualService." "Configure mTLS." Refer to Appendix D templates.
40 min~12Hard tasks: "Debug a broken mesh." "Fix egress." Use istioctl analyze + proxy-config.
15 min~17Review: Re-check EVERY answer. Verify commands actually worked. Leave nothing blank.
0 min~20DONE. Submit. Partial work earns partial credit — never leave a task blank.
⚠️ THE 7-MINUTE RULE: If you spend more than 7 minutes on any single task — STOP. Flag it, move to the next task, and return with fresh eyes. Getting stuck on one hard task costs you 3-4 easy tasks you could have completed.

❌ Top 10 Exam-Killing Mistakes

#MistakeFix
1Wrong Kubernetes contextRun kubectl config current-context as FIRST command in every task
2Forgetting to enable sidecar injectionkubectl label ns <ns> istio-injection=enabled BEFORE deploying pods
3Not restarting pods after labeling namespaceExisting pods NEVER get sidecars retroactively. kubectl rollout restart deploy
4VirtualService host doesn't match Service nameMust match EXACTLY. Short name OK if in same namespace.
5DestinationRule subsets use wrong label keysCheck: kubectl get pods --show-labels vs DR label selectors
6Gateway hosts mismatch VirtualService hostsMust match. "jobpost.com" ≠ "www.jobpost.com"
7TLS Secret in wrong namespaceGateway looks for Secret in Gateway's namespace, not istio-system
8ServiceEntry resolution: NONE breaks DNSAlways use resolution: DNS for external hostnames
9AuthorizationPolicy without sidecar does nothingAuthZ enforced by DESTINATION Envoy. Pod must be 2/2 READY.
10Typing YAML from scratchUse kubectl create ... $do > file.yaml then edit. Never type YAML.

🆘 Emergency Recovery — When Everything Is Broken

Panic Recovery Sequence (Run These IN ORDER)
  • ① Check istiod: kubectl get pods -n istio-system -l app=istiod — If not Running, nothing else matters.
  • ② Check proxy sync: istioctl proxy-status — STALE proxies = istiod can't reach sidecars.
  • ③ Analyze config: istioctl analyze -A — Finds 90% of configuration errors instantly.
  • ④ Restart control plane: kubectl rollout restart deploy/istiod -n istio-system
  • ⑤ Restart data plane: kubectl rollout restart deploy -n <ns> — Force sidecars to reconnect.
  • ⑥ Full diagnostic dump: istioctl bug-report — If all else fails, collect everything.

You know how to install Istio, configure traffic routing, secure workloads with mTLS and AuthZ, debug with istioctl and Envoy, and recover from mesh failures.

📚 Appendix I: Performance TuningPERF

⚡ Istio Performance Optimization — Resource Tuning, Sidecar Scoping & Benchmarking

Every sidecar adds ~50-100MB memory and ~0.5 vCPU overhead. At scale (100+ services), unoptimized Istio can consume significant cluster resources. This appendix covers Envoy resource tuning, sidecar config scoping, connection pool optimization, control plane scaling, and benchmarking methodology for production meshes.

50-100MB
Sidecar Memory (default)
~0.5 vCPU
Sidecar CPU (default)
2-8ms
Added Latency (p99)
~15MB
Sidecar Memory (scoped)

📐 Sidecar Resource Limits

# Global proxy defaults (IstioOperator)
apiVersion: install.istio.io/v1alpha1
kind: IstioOperator
spec:
  meshConfig:
    defaultConfig:
      proxyMetadata:
        # Reduce Envoy worker threads
        ISTIO_META_PROXY_XDS_CONCURRENCY: "2"
  values:
    global:
      proxy:
        resources:
          requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi}
          limits: {cpu: 200m, memory: 256Mi}
---
# Per-workload override (annotation)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        # Override for this specific workload
        sidecar.istio.io/proxyCPU: "100m"
        sidecar.istio.io/proxyMemory: "128Mi"
        sidecar.istio.io/proxyCPULimit: "500m"
        sidecar.istio.io/proxyMemoryLimit: "256Mi"

📦 Sidecar Scoping (Memory Saver)

# Limit sidecar to only what this workload needs
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: Sidecar
metadata: {name: anihpj-api-scope, namespace: anihpj}
spec:
  workloadSelector: {labels: {app: anihpj-api}}
  egress:
  - hosts:
    - "anihpj/*"        # All services in same ns
    - "istio-system/*"  # istiod + observability
    # WITHOUT scoping, sidecar sees ALL mesh services
    # 100 services = 100s of clusters = 100s of MB
    # WITH scoping: only 10-15 hosts = ~15MB sidecar

🔌 Connection Pool & Circuit Breaker Tuning

SettingDefaultLow TrafficMediumHigh Traffic
maxConnections10241005005000
http1MaxPendingRequests1024502001000
http2MaxRequests10241005005000
maxRequestsPerConnection0 (∞)1005000
connectTimeout10s5s10s30s

🎛️ istiod Control Plane Scaling

Mesh SizeProxiesistiod ReplicasCPU per istiodMemory per istiod
Small1-501500m1Gi
Medium50-200212Gi
Large200-500324Gi
X-Large500-1000548Gi
Enterprise1000+5+ HPA4+8Gi+
⚠️ Key Insight: istiod memory scales with NUMBER OF PROXIES × CONFIG SIZE. Each additional proxy adds ~2-5MB to istiod's memory. With 500 proxies and full mesh config, istiod can consume 4-8Gi. Use Sidecar resources to limit what each proxy sees — this reduces both proxy AND istiod memory.

📊 Benchmarking Methodology — Measure Before & After

Performance Test Checklist (Run for Each Change)
  • ① Baseline: Deploy workload WITHOUT sidecar. Measure latency (p50, p95, p99), throughput (RPS), CPU, memory.
  • ② With sidecar: Inject sidecar. Measure same metrics. Expected: +2-8ms p99 latency, +50-100MB memory.
  • ③ With mTLS STRICT: Enable mesh-wide STRICT. Measure again. Expected: minimal additional latency (~1ms for cached sessions).
  • ④ With AuthZ policies: Add AuthorizationPolicy rules. Expected: minimal impact (policy evaluation is in-memory).
  • ⑤ With observability: Enable access logging + Prometheus scraping. Measure logging overhead.
  • ⑥ After tuning: Apply Sidecar scoping + resource limits. Compare against baseline. Target: memory reduced by 60-80%.
# Quick benchmark from debug pod
kubectl run bench --rm -it --image=curlimages/curl --restart=Never -- \
  sh -c 'for i in $(seq 1 100); do
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n" http://anihpj-api.anihpj:8080/
  done' | awk '{sum+=$2; count++} END {print "Avg: " sum/count "s"}'

🔮 Future Trends — Where Service Mesh Is Heading

2025-2026 Service Mesh Trends
  • Ambient Mesh (Sidecar-less): Istio's ambient mode uses ztunnel (per-node, L4) + waypoint proxy (per-namespace, L7). Reduces resource overhead by 60-80% compared to sidecar-per-pod. This is the future of Istio.
  • eBPF-powered Networking: Cilium uses eBPF to enforce network policies at the kernel level — no sidecar needed. Istio is exploring eBPF integration for the data plane. Watch this space.
  • Gateway API Adoption: The Gateway API is replacing Ingress as the standard K8s networking API. Istio already supports it. Learning Gateway API is essential for future-proofing.
  • Platform Engineering: Companies are building Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs) that abstract mesh complexity. Understanding how to build self-service mesh platforms is the next career step.
  • AI/ML Traffic Management: Model serving requires specialized traffic routing (canary for models, A/B testing for prompts). Service mesh is becoming critical infrastructure for AI/ML platforms.
